body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "Another issue is setting pre drilled holes as starting points for some operations so we can dive down and do properly full depth cuts instead of trying to helix down little bit at a time..."

What is missing: a pocket or adaptive operation in closed material always works its own way down (helix or ramp), a little at a time. The usual shop method, drilling a start hole first and plunging the end mill down it to full depth, cannot be set up: the operation does not know a hole is there.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing operations, an "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group:
- Pick one or more points or existing drilled holes (a drilling operation earlier in the setup, a hole in the model, or a typed point with a diameter and depth).
- At such a position the tool goes straight down the hole at the plunge/rapid-in-clearance feed to the cutting depth and starts the full-depth cut from there, with no helix or ramp. Depth passes may then be full depth (the user's stepdown still rules).
- Regions with no entry position keep the helix or ramp, or are refused if the user chose "pre-drilled only".

Safety (this is a plunge into what the program believes is air):
- The hole must really be there when the operation runs: its source is an earlier operation in the same setup (or carried stock from a previous setup), checked against the stock simulation; a typed point with no drilling behind it is allowed only with the user's explicit "the hole exists" choice, shown in the operation summary and the setup sheet.
- The hole must be at least as wide as the tool plus a clearance and at least as deep as the plunge; otherwise refused by name with the numbers. A hole with a drill-point cone is counted only to its full-diameter depth.
- The entry must lie inside the region to cut, and the first sideways move starts from the hole wall, not from solid.
- The rapid-in-stock and gouge checks stay on: a plunge down a hole that the simulation does not show is refused at the post like any other.

Related: the companion issue on user-set start and exit points (filed with this one); tool kinds for drills are issue 897.

Done means: a closed pocket with a drilled start hole from an earlier operation plunges down the hole and cuts at full depth with no helix (golden CL, simulation clean); a hole too small or too shallow is refused by name in tests; a typed position without a drilling operation is refused unless the explicit choice is set; undo and redo; MCP parameters; the structural UI test covers the group.

Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

title: Process: every open process PR conflicts on .claude/PROCESS_VERSION each time another one merges

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Seen on 2026-11-12, a day with about 50 merges: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one integer that every process PR increments in its own branch. Each time one of them merges, every other open process PR either conflicts on that one line (GitHub shows CONFLICTING and the PR drops out of a merge run) or, worse, carries the SAME new number and merges cleanly - two process changes then share one number and a fork that already synced at it never pulls the second (it happened with #1117 and #930 at 17; fixed by the extra bump PR #1142). Today #965, #967, #972, #1033, #1024, #1100, #1116 and #1151 all had to be renumbered by hand, some more than once.

The law today (AGENTS.md "Process changes bump PROCESS_VERSION"): the PR increments the number; "whichever merges second takes the next number when it merges main".

Proposal to decide (maintainer): the number is not written in the PR at all. A process PR only says in its body "process change: yes" (the reviewer checks that instead of the bump); the merging session increments `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` right after the merge in a one-line follow-up PR (or the merge tooling does: `cargo xtask process-bump`), and posts the #681 announcement with that number. One writer, no conflicts, no shared numbers. Alternatives: derive the version from the count of merge commits touching the process paths (no file at all), or keep the file and make `.gitattributes` resolve it with a custom "max + 1" merge driver (needs local git config on every clone, so probably not).

Done means: the chosen rule is in AGENTS.md (and the review-prs / merge-ready skills), two process PRs open at once no longer conflict with each other, and two of them can never land on the same number; `PROCESS_VERSION` bumped and announced for this change itself.

title: Carry machined stock into a setup turned side-on (90° about X or Y)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: P4

body:
Part of #866. Related: #637 (carried stock on the field engine), #586.

**What the reporter wanted:** a plate modelled lying flat; Setup1 machines it flat, Setup2 stands it on its edge (part alignment "turned X -90°") and takes "What Setup1 leaves behind" as its stock. Today that carry is refused by design (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`): the carried body is a two-sided column lattice (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`, `LatticeTurn`), which can only be re-indexed through flips over X or Y and quarter turns about Z. A side-on turn would need a re-sample at the grid pitch, and the sim refuses rather than guess.

Investigation for #866 confirmed the frame composition is right: `setup_relative::transform_between` uses the RELATIVE turn (`A_to * A_from^-1`), so two setups holding the part alike (both turned X -90°) carry fine (pinned by `setup_stock_source::both_setups_turned_alike_carry_through_the_identity`). Only a real side-on turn between the setups is refused.

**The work:** carry the machined stock through any rigid turn between setups (at least the side-on quarter turns about X and Y - the common "machine the edge" re-clamp), once the carried body lives on the field engine (#637), with the verdicts proven exact enough and the named refusal kept for anything the engine still cannot carry.

**Done means:** Setup1 flat, Setup2 turned 90° about X (or Y) with "What Setup1 leaves behind" simulates, judges gouges and feeds rest/judged stock from the carried body; a pinning test carries a faced plate side-on and checks its volume and verdict.

title: One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

labels.name: area:multiaxis

body:
# One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

## What

The part-alignment machinery (#326) and the per-operation tilt frame (the
3+2 index, M5.1 B) both exist and both work — but only separately.
`setup_align::generation_problem` allows generation in an aligned setup for
exactly four kinds (Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive), and tilt
inside an aligned setup is refused outright. Every other planar kind,
picks, and area controls are refused by name. The refusals are a
verification gap, not a mathematical one: the two mechanisms compose as
plain function composition.

This issue builds ONE seam — `OpFrame`, `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs`
— that composes the two existing mechanisms and becomes the single door
the generators' world reads go through. No generator rewrites: the motion
generators take data (facets, regions, heights); only the app read/wrap
seam moves.

## The frame contract

Coordinate systems:

- **D** — document frame (as modelled). Part entities carry their
  `Location` in D.
- **S** — setup frame: the table frame, also the world the CL stream and
  the post speak. Stock, WCS and fixtures are setup FURNITURE — stored in
  S already (#326's law; their world reads are correct and stay untouched).
- **L** — local machining frame: XY = the cutting plane, +Z = the tool
  axis. Exists only when the op tilts.

Point maps (right-to-left application, the `setup_align::compose`
convention):

- D → S: `A` = the setup's `part_alignment`, baked into part geometry
  reads (`facets_in` and siblings). Never inverted — the CL never maps
  back to D.
- S → L: `T` = `TiltedFrame` from `op.params.tilt()` (`to_local`), applied
  AFTER the alignment read: `p_L = T(A(p_D))`.
- L → S (CL out): `T.to_world`, the tilt's inverse. The whole CL stream
  wraps through `TiltedFrame::world_path`; identity when no tilt exists.

Layers stay separate (never a fourth):

1. part_alignment — setup, physical (how the part is clamped)
2. WCS — program zero (translation today)
3. operation tool orientation — the `Tilt` param

Machine-side relations remain derived internal transforms composed from
these; no user-facing SCS, no second offset frame.

## Design conditions (from the plan review)

1. **Heights and bounding boxes resolve against fully transformed
   geometry** (local bounds of `T(A(f))`), never a bare `z − origin.z`
   shift — a Z shift is not generally correct for an arbitrarily tilted
   plane. `OpFrame`'s height and AABB reads implement this from day one.
2. **Machine capability gates are preserved and pinned by tests**: a
   tilted orientation never silently posts as plain XYZ when the machine
   cannot reach it. The post's tilted-record refusals (non-RTCP, no
   rotary) keep their verdicts.
3. **Stepwise integration**: Phase 1 wires the seam behind the four
   currently-supported kinds, byte-identical. Refusals lift only as their
   numeric tests land: picks in aligned setups next, then further 2D/3D
   families, alignment × tilt last.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 (first branch)**: `OpFrame` + the four kinds through it,
  behavior byte-identical; the seam's math pinned by unit tests (identity,
  90°/180° alignment, alignment × tilt composition, transformed picks,
  local heights on tilted planes, AABBs under arbitrary rotation, CL
  back-transform, tool direction, capability gates, byte-identity).
- **Phase 2**: the selection walk reads picked parts through the seam
  (`facets_in`); picks in aligned setups verified. Tilt × picks stays
  refused.
- **Phase 3**: `verified_kind` extended kind by kind (whole-model 3D
  kinds first), each with a pinned numeric test; area controls; then tilt
  × alignment.
- **Phase 4**: re-evaluate #760 (rotated-offset carry) on top of the
  unified seam — normal 3-axis work needs alignment coverage, not offset
  rotation.

## Done means (Phase 1)

- `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` exists with the contract above;
  `collect_job` reads geometry/heights for the four kinds through it.
- The mandatory test list above is green.
- Existing aligned-setup tests (#326's) and goldens pass unchanged —
  byte-identical output.
- No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.

Related: #326 (part alignment), #316 (setup-to-setup transform), #315
(rotation refusal at the post), #760 (rotated-offset carry — re-evaluated
in phase 4, untouched by this issue's branches).

body:
Reported by the maintainer while hand-testing the setup page's part alignment (screenshot of the Setups page attached in chat: Part alignment dropdown at the top, then "Lay on a plane - pick a face", "pick three points", "Axes in the plane - pick an edge or two points").

## What's wrong

1. **The "Part alignment" control at the top overrides the pickers.** The dropdown and the Turn X/Y/Z + about + Apply row sit above the face, three-point and edge/two-point pickers, and applying one wipes out what the others did. It's unclear which one is in charge. The page should read as one flow, where the pickers are the way to align and the preset/turn row doesn't silently override them (or is clearly a separate "start from a preset" step).
2. **Each pick-driven move resets the part and then moves it.** Laying on a face, on three points or applying axes first returns the body to its import pose and then applies only the new transform. Expected: each move applies **to the body as it is now** (incremental, composed with what was done before), and undo steps back one move at a time.
3. **Pick status shows internal ids.** "Face 0xccc7c…" (the welded-face id) means nothing to a user. Show the count and the kind: "1 face selected", "2 points selected", "1 edge selected".
4. **Picked geometry is hard to see.**
   - **Faces:** only the outline is drawn in purple. Fill the whole picked face with the pick colour (semi-transparent), so it's obvious which face it is.
   - **Vertices / points:** draw them as round, visible markers (filled discs, somewhat transparent is fine), not a speck.
   - **Edges:** the picked edge line is so thin it barely shows against the grey part. Draw it noticeably thicker (bold).

## Related
- #692 (one picking rule for the whole app: what is pickable). This issue is about how picks are *shown* and how the alignment page *applies* them.
- #330, #555, #557, #606 (lay on a face, three-point plane, axes by edge/two points, align about the WCS origin): the features this page combines.
- #701 (WCS from picked features with roles).

## Done means
- Applying a face, three-point or axis alignment moves the part from its current pose; a pinning test applies two alignments in a row and checks the second composes on the first, and undo restores each step.
- The top "Part alignment" preset/turn row no longer silently discards a picker's result (pinned by a test, or the page is restructured so the two can't conflict); the flow is described in the page's tooltips.
- Pick status reads "N face(s)/edge(s)/point(s) selected", with no internal ids (structural test).
- Picked faces are filled with the pick colour, picked points are round markers, and picked edges are drawn bold. Checked by the structural/paint assertions where they can be, hand-tested by the maintainer otherwise (no snapshot PNG changes in the PR).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

body:
Found while fixing #510 (PR #513). The shared level helper `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts every depth-stepping ladder at Top: pocket, contour, circular, trace, face, slot and the 3D entries. When Top is the material's top surface, which is the default for most 2D ops, the first level is a full feed pass in air. For example, a Slot with top 20, bottom 10 and step 5 cuts at [20, 15, 10]. That's never a gouge, but it's a wasted pass at feed rate on every op.

**Question for the owner:** should the first level be `top - step` (giving [15, 10]), or should an air pass be skipped only when Top is at the material top?

Either change moves most CL and NC goldens, so it should be one deliberate change across every ladder, not per op.

Done means: a decision recorded; if yes, every ladder starts one step below Top (or skips the air level), goldens are regenerated in one commit, and the change is pinned by a ladder test.
